transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate it. 

Um... well, I was actually sent here by occupational health at my job. I run presses and do metal fabrication all day, and... well, they told me they think my weight has gotten dangerously low for that kind of heavy work. 

I hope I'm not wasting your time, though, because I honestly just thought I was getting a bit leaner, you know? Just being more disciplined with myself and my routine. Does that make sense? I really didn't mean to cause any trouble or worry anyone at work.
Did you intentionally try to lose weight?

Um... I wouldn't say I was trying to lose weight, exactly. I just... I wanted to be more structured, I guess? I hope that doesn't sound silly. I just really like having a routine, it helps me do a good job at work. 

So, most days, I just keep it to coffee before my early shift starts. And then maybe... maybe half a protein bar at lunch. And then just a small bowl of vegetables after I do my yoga in the evening. I know it probably sounds like I'm not eating much, and I'm sorry if that's the wrong way to do things, but... eating more than that just makes the whole day feel sort of out of control? Like I'm letting myself go. 

I just wanted to be good and stay on top of things. Is that... do you know what I mean?
Do you think you would still limit your food intake even if you weren't trying to follow a routine?

Um... gosh, I'm really not sure. I haven't really thought about it like that, to be honest. 

I just... I've had my schedule for so long now, it's hard to picture not having it, you know? I guess... I don't know. Maybe I wouldn't? Or maybe I'd just find a different way to stay organized. I hope that's an okay answer... I just honestly haven't tried going without my structure lately. Does that make sense?
Do you think you are at a healthy weight right now?

Um... well, I honestly feel like I'm doing okay? I hope it's alright for me to say that. 

I know my family keeps saying I look sick, and I feel just terrible for worrying them... and the shop nurse, she acted like it was this huge emergency when she sent me here. I was so embarrassed to cause a fuss like that. 

But I keep telling them... and I hope you understand where I'm coming from... I'm still working double shifts at the presses, and I'm still running, and getting all my chores and everything done. So... it just really can't be as serious as they're making it out to be, right? I mean, if I was actually at a dangerous weight, I wouldn't be able to keep up with all that heavy work and exercise, would I? 

I just... I hope I'm not being difficult or stubborn by seeing it that way. Does that make sense to you?
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Um... well... I guess maybe a little bit? I hope you don't think I'm being vain or anything. It's not really about looks, it's just... 

I just get so nervous if I see the scale go up. Even just a tiny bit. It feels like... like I'm losing my grip on everything I've worked so hard to keep organized. I just panic that I'm going to lose all that control and... and end up heavy again. 

I know that probably sounds silly, worrying over a pound or two. I try not to let it get to me, I really do. I just want to keep things steady, you know? I hope that's a normal way to feel about it... is it?
Is your fear of gaining weight the main reason you restrict your food intake?

Um... I suppose the fear of gaining weight is part of it, yes. But honestly, it's really more about just... keeping everything manageable? I hope that doesn't sound too strange. 

It's just that... well, most days I try to keep it to just some black coffee before my early shift at the plant, and then... maybe half a protein bar on my lunch break. And then just a small bowl of vegetables after I do my yoga in the evening. I know that probably sounds like I should be having more, and I really hope you're not disappointed with me for doing it this way. 

It's just... if I try to eat more than that, the whole day just feels completely out of control. Like I'm messing up my whole system and everything is going to fall apart. Keeping it small and strict just helps me feel like I have a handle on things, you know? Is it okay that I need it to be predictable like that?
Would you say that your fear of gaining weight is one of the most important things on your mind most of the time?

Um... well... I guess it is on my mind a lot. I really hope you don't think I'm just being shallow or obsessed with my appearance. It's just... 

Well, when I'm walking past the shop windows at the plant, or even just washing my hands in the bathroom mirror... I catch a glimpse of myself, and my eyes just immediately go straight to my stomach and my thighs. And... they just look so big to me. 

I know I shouldn't let it bother me so much, and I feel silly even admitting this... but seeing that can just completely ruin my mood for the rest of the day. It makes me feel so bad about myself. I try to just put my head down and get back to work, but it's hard to shake that feeling. I hope that doesn't make me sound terribly vain... does everyone worry about things like that sometimes?
Do you think you would still see yourself as overweight even if someone told you that you are at a healthy weight?

Um... well... I guess I'm not really sure? I mean, if a doctor told me I was healthy, I would definitely want to believe them. I really would. I know you're the expert and I trust your judgment. 

It's just... sometimes it's hard for me to see what other people see, I think. Even if someone said I was fine, I might still look in the mirror and... and just feel like I'm taking up too much space. But I would try really hard to listen to you if you told me I was at a good weight. I don't want to be difficult or disagree with you. I hope it doesn't make me a bad patient if I struggle to see it myself... is it normal to have a hard time believing it?
Do you think your fear of gaining weight is what makes you see yourself as overweight?

Um... I'm really not sure. I hope it doesn't frustrate you that I don't have a better answer for that. 

I guess... maybe they are connected? I mean, I do worry about gaining weight, like I said, and I do feel like I look too big. But I don't know if one causes the other, or if it's just... how I am? 

I really try not to overthink it too much, because I don't want to make things more complicated than they need to be. I just want to do whatever is right. Do you... do you think that's what's happening? I'd really value your opinion on it, since you understand these things so much better than I do.
Do you think you would still see yourself as overweight if you were at the same weight as your friends or peers?

Um... well, honestly... I think I probably would still feel that way, even if I weighed the same as the other women at the plant. I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds so irrational. 

It's just like I mentioned before... when I walk past the shop windows at work, or when I'm washing my hands in the bathroom... I just catch that glimpse of myself, and my eyes just lock right onto my stomach and my thighs. And... they just look so heavy to me. It doesn't seem to matter what anyone else weighs, it's just what I see when I look at myself. 

And it's so silly, but seeing that... it really can just ruin how I feel about myself for the whole rest of my shift. I try so hard to just smile and be pleasant with everyone, but inside I just feel... big. I really hope you don't think I'm just being difficult or completely obsessed with myself. I want to see things normally, I really do. Is it... is it okay that I feel that way, even if it doesn't make logical sense?
Do you think your fear of gaining weight contributes to why you see yourself as overweight?

Um... I think you might have just asked me that? Or maybe I misunderstood... I'm so sorry if I'm getting confused, I don't mean to make you repeat yourself. 

But, um... like I was saying before, I really don't know for sure if the fear is what causes it. I guess it makes sense when you put it that way? I mean, I definitely do worry about it, and I definitely feel like I look too big. I just... I'm not really sure how it all works in my head. 

I hope that's an okay answer... I know it's not very helpful. I just really want to give you the right information so you can help me. Do you think that's what's going on with me? I really trust your opinion on this.
Do you think your weight and body shape are the most important things to you when you think about your overall health and well-being?

Um... I really hope it doesn't sound too vain or shallow when I say this... but yes, I think they probably are. 

I'm so sorry to keep bringing up the same thing, I really don't want to bore you or sound like a broken record, but... it just goes back to what I was saying a minute ago about the shop windows and the bathroom mirror at work. When I catch sight of myself and all I can focus on is my stomach and my thighs looking too big... it just completely takes over. It ruins how I feel about myself for the rest of the day, and it's hard to think about any other part of my health when I'm feeling that way. 

I know I shouldn't let it dictate my whole well-being, and I know that's probably not the right way a person should think about their health. I really do try to care about other things, I promise. Is it... is it terrible that I let it affect me that much? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the most honest answer I can so you can help me. Does that make sense?
Do you think you would still be afraid of gaining weight if you didn't think you looked overweight?

Um... well, honestly... I think I probably would still be afraid. 

I know that sounds a bit silly, since I just said how much seeing myself looking heavy bothers me. But... it's just that I've worked so, so hard to keep things where they are. I try to be so careful. And if I step on the scale and it goes up, even just a tiny bit... I just get this awful feeling of panic. 

It's like... I worry that if I let it slip even a little, I'll just lose all the control I've tried so hard to maintain, and I'll end up heavy again. I'm so sorry, I know that probably sounds terribly obsessive. I really don't mean to be that way, I just get so scared of losing control. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your questions the right way.
Do you think your fear of gaining weight is related to how you think you look, rather than your actual weight?

Um... I think you might be right? Or, I mean, I guess I haven't really thought about it exactly like that before... 

I'm sorry, I hope I'm not being difficult by not having a clear answer. I just... I know my actual weight on the scale is low, because you and my regular doctor have told me it is, and I know I shouldn't argue with that. But when I look in the mirror, I just see something so different, and that's what terrifies me. 

So maybe it is more about how I think I look? I just... I don't want to say the wrong thing and mislead you. I know my mind plays tricks on me sometimes with this stuff. Do you think that's what's happening? I'll agree with whatever you think is most accurate, I just really want to be a good patient and help you figure this out.
Is your fear of gaining weight the main reason you eat so little?

Um... well, I guess... yes, that fear is definitely a big part of it. I really hope you don't think I'm doing this just to be difficult or stubborn. I'm really not. 

It's just... I try to be really careful, you know? Like, most days I'll just have coffee before my early shift at the plant, and then maybe half of a protein bar on my lunch break. And then after work, if I go to yoga, I'll just have a small bowl of vegetables. 

I know it probably sounds like I'm not doing a good job taking care of myself, and I'm so sorry if that's frustrating to hear. But... if I eat more than that, the whole day just feels completely out of control, and that fear just takes over. I really do try to do the right thing, though. Is... is it okay that I'm telling you this? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Is your fear of gaining weight the only reason you restrict your food intake to so little?

Um... honestly, I think it probably is the only reason. I can't really think of anything else... I hope that's an okay answer. 

I know it's probably silly for a grown woman to be so hung up on this, especially working in a shop with a bunch of guys who just eat whatever they want all day. I really try not to make a big deal out of it at work or bother anyone with it. But... yeah, it's really just that fear of getting heavy and losing control. 

I don't think there's any other deep reason behind it, or at least not that I've noticed. Is... is that what you were asking? I'm sorry if I'm not being very helpful or if you were looking for something more specific. I really am trying to give you the right answers.
Is your fear of gaining weight the main reason you limit your food intake to the extent that you do?

Um... yes, I think we just talked about that, but... yes, it really is the main reason. I'm sorry, I hope I didn't confuse you before or make it seem like I was hiding something else. 

I just... I really want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to help me. I know I'm probably repeating myself, and I don't want to waste your time. But yes, that fear is really the driving force behind it all. I hope it's okay that I don't have a better or more complicated answer for you. Am I doing okay? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.
Do you think your fear of gaining weight would decrease if you had a more accurate perception of your body shape and weight?

Um... I don't know. I've never really thought about it like that. I guess... maybe? 

I mean, I look in the mirror and I just see what I see. I don't really feel like I have a distorted view or anything, I just... I know what I want to look like, and I know I'm not there. I hope that doesn't sound too crazy or vain. I really try not to be obsessed with it, honestly. 

But... if I saw myself differently, would the fear go away? I'm not sure. I think the fear is just always there, no matter what. Does that make sense? I'm sorry, I feel like I'm not giving you a very good answer. I just want to make sure I'm understanding you right. Is that what you meant?
Do you think your fear of gaining weight would change if you could see your body the way others see it?

Um... I guess that's kind of like what you just asked, right? About having a different perception of my body? 

I... I don't know if seeing it the way others do would change the fear. People at the shop sometimes tell me I look fine, or even that I'm too thin, but... I just assume they're being nice, you know? They're good guys, they don't want to hurt my feelings. 

If I actually saw what they saw... I'm really not sure. I think I'd still just be terrified of getting big. It's like the fear is just baked into me at this point. I hope I'm not being difficult by not having a straight yes or no for you. I'm really trying to think it through... is it okay that I'm just not sure?
